title: Sell Mineral Rights in Buffalo, OH
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Buffalo, OH | Guernsey County
metaDescription: Own mineral rights near Buffalo, Guernsey County, along the I-70 corridor? Learn how nearby midstream infrastructure affects value, then get a cash offer.
heroLead: Buffalo sits in Guernsey County near the I-70 corridor, an area that's benefited from both highway access and the midstream buildout tied to Utica development.
intro: Guernsey County's position along Interstate 70 made it a natural hub for the infrastructure that shale gas needs to get to market, gathering lines, compressor stations, and processing capacity built out over the past decade. If your family owns minerals near Buffalo, that infrastructure is part of why development in this part of the county has been fairly consistent rather than sporadic.

The unincorporated community sits inside the Utica core, and much of the surrounding farmland has been under lease, in some cases multiple leases across different ownership eras, for over ten years now.

sections.heading: Why infrastructure access matters to your bottom line
paragraphs: A well can be productive underground and still generate inconsistent royalty payments if the gas has nowhere efficient to go. Guernsey County's midstream buildout near the I-70 corridor has generally supported more reliable takeaway capacity, which tends to translate into steadier production reporting on your royalty statement rather than gaps caused by pipeline constraints.

sections.heading: Confirming ownership near Buffalo
paragraphs: Guernsey County deed and lease records are held at the recorder's office in Cambridge. Because Buffalo is unincorporated, mineral title work here follows the same township-and-section legal description system as the rest of the county, not a separate municipal record.
If your interest is producing, your division order will list the specific well and unit name, which is the fastest way to confirm current status.

sections.heading: If your tract hasn't been leased
paragraphs: Not every parcel near Buffalo has been picked up yet, even in an active county like Guernsey. If that's your situation, an offer is built from comparable nearby leasing and development activity rather than existing production, and it's worth checking with the county recorder to confirm whether a lease offer has ever been extended on your specific tract, since older correspondence sometimes gets misplaced over the years.

faqs.question: Why does infrastructure near I-70 matter for my royalty?
faqs.answer: Reliable gathering and processing capacity generally supports steadier production reporting, which affects both your royalty consistency and how a buyer values the interest.

faqs.question: Is Buffalo, being unincorporated, harder to research than a city?
faqs.answer: No, all mineral records are tracked by legal description at the county level regardless of whether the community is incorporated.

faqs.question: What if I'm not sure whether my tract was ever leased?
faqs.answer: A search at the Guernsey County Recorder's office in Cambridge will confirm whether any lease has been recorded against your specific legal description.
